key_idea: Tokenise each line into name(arg,...) records ignoring whitespace, then match every query against facts of the same name and arity with per-query variable bindings.
sketch: Parse facts by scanning for a name, then '(' and collecting names until ')'; several facts may sit on one line with or without separating whitespace. Store facts in a map keyed by (name, arity). For a query, iterate over that bucket: a literal must equal the fact argument, '_' matches anything, and a named variable binds on first use and must equal the bound value on later uses (different variables may bind to the same name). Count every occurrence, including duplicates. At most ~10^4 facts and 200 queries, so brute force is trivial. Pitfalls: the fact section ends at a blank (possibly whitespace-only) line, names can be all digits, whitespace may appear between the name and '('.
